subject: RESOLVED: mirt.model error while defining covariance terms

messages.author: b08b7e19b674e717
messages.subject: Re: mirt.model error while defining covariance terms
parts: Thanks Phil for helping me resolve this issue ! The solution is to update the package to the recent development version, where this issue has been resolved.

On Thursday, May 15, 2014 3:45:44 PM UTC-5, Nishant Verma wrote:
Hi Phil,

First of all, I would like to say thank you for all your efforts in developing this package and making it available to the R community. After having tried several item response theory related packages, I think this is currently one of the best resources available in R.

While the exploratory IRT modeling works perfectly, I have been facing one problem in the confirmatory IRT analysis. In my analysis, I am considering >3 latent factors for exploring the relationships between 32 categorical (both binary and ordinal) items on a large data (~3000 observations). The latent factors are expected to be correlated with each other. Therefore, while defining the confirmatory model, I need to include covariance terms between the factors. However, I keep getting an error when I consider the estimation method to be EM. For better understanding, I am including the code and the error that is returned:

> Conf_IRT_F3_Model_2 <- mirt.model('F1 = 1, 20-27, 32, 11-19, 31
+                                 F2 = 2-13, 28-31, 17-19
+                                 F3 = 11-19
+                                 COV = F1*F2, F2*F3, F1*F3')
> Conf_IRT_F3_2 <- mirt(ADAS_Model, model = Conf_IRT_F3_Model_2,
+                       method = "EM", rotate = "oblimin",
+                       technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000, MAXQUAD= 20000))
Iteration: 3, Log-Lik: -55881.088, Max-Change: 0.55864
Error in Mstep(pars = pars, est = est, longpars = longpars, ngroups = ngroups,  : 
  Error in optim(p, fn = Mstep.LL, gr = Mstep.grad, method = "L-BFGS-B",  : 
  L-BFGS-B needs finite values of 'fn'
In addition: Warning message:
In log(eigen(sigma, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values) :
  NaNs produced

If I perform this analysis using MHRM, it works fine. However, the obtained estimates are not as accurate as obtained from EM. Therefore, I want to perform this analysis using EM method. I have tried increasing the number of quadrature points to 25 but it still gives the same error. The relationships of the factors with the items (as defined above) is determined by first performing the exploratory IRT modeling. The latent factors from exploratory IRT phase show ~0.50 correlation with each other. Do you have any insight into what may be the possible reason behind this error ? 

Thank you,
Nishant
